title: Divide fractions
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

sections.title: How many fit?
sections.objective: Understand dividing as "how many of these fit into that?"
explain: 12 ÷ 3 asks: how many 3s fit into 12? Dividing by a fraction asks the same thing. 4 ÷ {1/3} asks: how many thirds fit into 4?
Each whole has 3 thirds, so 4 wholes have 4 × 3 = 12 thirds. So 4 ÷ {1/3} = 12. Dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a bigger answer, because small pieces fit many times.
For 6 ÷ {2/3}: 6 wholes are 18 thirds, and each {2/3} uses 2 of them. 18 ÷ 2 = 9.
For {3/4} ÷ {1/8}: write {3/4} in eighths. {3/4} = {6/8}, so 6 eighths fit.

visual.caption: Cut each whole into thirds and count the pieces.

sections.title: Reciprocals
sections.objective: Flip a fraction or a whole number to get its reciprocal.
explain: The reciprocal of a fraction is the fraction flipped: the top and bottom swap. The reciprocal of {3/5} is {5/3}.
A whole number is a fraction over 1: 4 = {4/1}, so its reciprocal is {1/4}. And the reciprocal of {1/6} is {6/1}, which is 6.
A number times its reciprocal is always 1: {3/5} × {5/3} = {15/15} = 1. Write a reciprocal as a fraction (like {5/3}), not a mixed number.

sections.title: Divide by flipping
sections.objective: Divide by multiplying by the reciprocal of the second number.
explain: Dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. 12 ÷ 2 and 12 × {1/2} are both 6.
So: keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second. {2/3} ÷ {4/5} = {2/3} × {5/4} = {10/12}, which simplifies to {5/6}.
Flip only the second number, the one you're dividing by. Flipping the first one, or not flipping at all, gives a different answer.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Divide fractions and whole numbers, and write each answer in simplest form.
explain: Write any whole number over 1. Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, flip the second. Then multiply and simplify.

hints.frac.divide.meaning: Count in the small pieces: how many of those pieces are in the first number? Then how many pieces does each group use?
hints.frac.divide.reciprocal: Swap the top and the bottom. A whole number is that number over 1.
hints.frac.divide.multiply-reciprocal: Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, flip the second number. Then multiply.
hints.frac.divide: Keep, change, flip: keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, flip the second. Then multiply and simplify.

simplifyHint: That's the right amount, but it isn't in simplest form yet. Is there a number that still divides both the top and the bottom?

misconceptionMessages.frac.div-no-flip: It looks like you multiplied without flipping. When you change ÷ to ×, flip the second number.
misconceptionMessages.frac.div-flip-first: Flip the second number (the one you divide by), not the first.
misconceptionMessages.frac.div-meaning-multiplied: That's {1/3} of the amount. The question asks how many pieces fit, so count the pieces: each whole has as many pieces as the bottom number.
misconceptionMessages.frac.recip-same: The reciprocal is the number flipped over: swap the top and the bottom.
